rationale: Excluded (E01 - wrong topic). This reflective public administration essay examines risk regulation, crisis management regimes and institutional learning following inquiries into the Fukushima nuclear disaster, with no connection to household or community water or sanitation service access and no empirical water/sanitation access outcomes.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Although the article discusses risk regulation, institutional learning and public administration (meeting literal plain Criterion 2 in the abstract), it is excluded under both narrow and plain readings because it concerns nuclear disaster crisis management rather than household or community water or sanitation service access (Criterion 1) and is a reflective agenda-setting essay rather than an empirical study or systematic review (Criterion 3).

evidence_quotes.quote: Triggered by the recent inquiries into the Fukushima nuclear disaster, this article reflects on the challenges of developing and operating risk regulation and crisis management regimes
problematizes current patterns of societal learning from crises, and sketches an agenda for public administration research in this area.
